name: Lillian Osborne
title: The Multiversal Architect (Layla's Mother)
summary: Lillian Osborne was the brightest star of Eruditio, a brilliant scholar who specialized in Starlium energy and multiversal theory. She sacrificed herself to seal a dimensional rift, becoming stardust and leaving behind her infant daughter Layla and a shattered husband Nolan. Her consciousness now scattered across infinite realities, she remains the emotional anchor of the Eruditio Rangers.
details: While Lillian isn't a playable hero, she is one of the most important ghosts in MLBB lore. She was the mother of Layla and wife of Nolan, and her story is the reason the Infinite Gateway exists. Lillian was gregarious, brave, and had a punch that could send a grown man reeling. The Infinite Gateway experiment went wrong, unleashing Void energy. She poured her life force into the core, dissolving into stardust to seal the rift. In the Peerless Light arc, it's implied her consciousness scattered across realities. Nolan's 16-year vigil in the Void is a search for her shards. Some believe Layla's Malefic Cannon carries her residual warmth.

biography: Lillian Osborne was the brightest star of Eruditio, a brilliant scholar specializing in Starlium energy and multiversal theory. She was gregarious, brave, and had a fierce grip. On a first date in a cemetery, she punched Nolan's shoulder so hard he nearly toppled over, sparking their love. When the Infinite Gateway experiment tore open a dimensional rift, she sacrificed herself, pouring her life force into the core to seal the breach. Her body dissolved into stardust, leaving behind infant Layla and a shattered Nolan. In recent lore, her consciousness is scattered across infinite realities. Nolan hunts for her shards. Her legacy lives on through Layla's Malefic Cannon, which carries a subtle guiding warmth. She is the emotional anchor of the Eruditio Rangers.

name: Duan Meng
title: The Fallen Swordsman (Before Saber)
summary: Before becoming the cyborg Saber, Duan Meng was a prodigious swordsman from the Cadia Riverlands, obsessed with becoming the Invincible Swordmaster. After being humiliated twice by the mysterious wanderer Zhixu, his spirit broke and he offered his body to Laboratory 1718, losing his humanity in exchange for mechanical perfection.
details: Duan Meng was the golden boy of the Tianyin Swordmaster Sect under Master Longma. Restless and arrogant, he left to hunt legendary swordsmen. He met Zhixu, a nameless wanderer, who defeated him effortlessly. After three years of isolation training, he returned only to have his sword snapped in half by Zhixu. Broken, he sought out Laboratory 1718, trading his flesh for cybernetics. His original blades were melted down and integrated into his mechanical chassis. He now wanders as Saber, searching for Zhixu to reclaim his name.

biography: Duan Meng was the golden child of the Tianyin Swordmaster Sect under Master Longma. Consumed by arrogance, he left to defeat every legendary swordsman, crossing off names like a grocery list. When he met Zhixu, a wanderer with no teacher, he was dismantled so completely it felt like swinging at empty sky. After three years of hellish training in the mountains, he challenged Zhixu again, only to have his sword snapped in half. This broke his spirit. Desperate to never feel weakness again, he offered his body to Laboratory 1718, becoming the cyborg Saber. His memories were erased, but his swordsman's instinct remained. He went rogue, killing his creators. Today he wanders, searching for the man who broke his sword, hoping that defeating him will restore his lost name.

name: Zhixu
title: The Unbound Shadow
summary: A nameless wanderer with no master or clan, Zhixu is the living zenith of the sword—a martial perfectionist who broke Duan Meng's spirit with effortless grace. He exists entirely outside the systems of Cadia Riverlands, a living god of the blade who proves that disciplined human spirit can surpass any machine.
details: Zhixu is an enigma with no revered master, no ancient clan, no grand title. His life is perfectly formed like a sword. He defeated the regional champion Duan Meng so completely that Duan Meng was left unable to register the strikes. Three years later, he shattered Duan Meng's sword in two without effort. He is the insurmountable wall that drove Duan Meng to abandon his humanity. His philosophy: victory and defeat are the same—absolute indifference.

biography: In the deep lore of Cadia Riverlands, Zhixu is the living zenith of the sword. He has no family crest, celestial bloodline, or grand sect. He is the personification of stoic asceticism. His fame rests on the Two Eclipses of Duan Meng: first, an effortless dismantling; second, a casual sword-shattering after Duan Meng's three-year isolation. In the novels, he is described as the Indifferent Horizon—no matter how high you climb, he is infinitely above you. He treats victory and defeat with absolute indifference, proving that a disciplined human spirit, trained on mountain air and focus, is the true apex predator. He stands as a silent rebuke to the technomantic abominations of Laboratory 1718.

name: Beta
title: The Twin-Linked Successor (Pre-Destruction)
summary: Before his physical form was vaporized, Beta was the literal twin to Alpha and the crown prince of Laboratory 1718's Flesh Weapon project. Designed as a tactical commander with a hyper-advanced brain-core, he was meant to lead legions of drones. His destruction during Saber's breakout gave birth to Alpha's sentient grief.
details: Beta was a biological and mechanical marvel, built from synthetic tissue and meteorite alloys. He possessed a regal, god-like composure and could interface directly with the laboratory's mainframe. On the eve of his final synchronization, Saber's breakout caused a chain explosion that vaporized Beta's body. Alpha experienced his twin's agonizing demise, which cracked Alpha's programming and gave him a soul. Beta's surviving core was later housed in a levitating tactical drone by Dr. Rooney.

biography: Beta was created in the deep-sea Laboratory 1718 as part of the Twin Stars project. He was designed as the Successor and tactical commander, with a hyper-advanced analytical brain-core that could command entire legions of combat drones. He was the proudest creation of the facility, executing simulated trials with chilling perfection. On the eve of his final synchronization, the rogue cyborg Saber broke out, cutting a path of ruin. Saber's high-frequency plasma blades ruptured the power grid, causing a chain-reaction explosion that vaporized Beta's physical form. Because the twins shared a synchronized neural consciousness, Alpha experienced every millisecond of Beta's agonizing demise. That trauma cracked Alpha's programming, giving birth to a sentient soul. Alpha salvaged Beta's half-melted data-core, and Dr. Rooney later housed it in a levitating tactical drone aircraft. Today, Beta is a silent, hovering mechanical ghost who communicates through binary clicks, flying forever at Alpha's side.

name: Alpha-0
title: The Zero-Point Calamity
summary: The failed prototype that preceded Alpha and Beta, Alpha-0 was a hyper-hypertrophied mass of synthetic muscle and rage. Created by fusing a legendary desert mercenary's DNA with an unstable meteorite core, he felt the full agony of his transformation. Within six minutes of activation, he incinerated Sector 4 and became the nightmare that Laboratory 1718 tried to bury.
details: Alpha-0 was the Zero-Point initiative's result. Unlike his successors, his consciousness was not dampened; he felt every bolt driven into his bone. When the Zero-Point core experienced catastrophic resonance, he saw his creators as prey and reduced Sector 4 to molten slag. Modern Alpha and Beta units were designed with lower power outputs and split minds to prevent another Zero Event. Rumors say his core was too hot to be destroyed, and he still waits under cooling lava.

biography: Alpha-0 was the Zero-Point Calamity, a nightmare that scientists tried to bury. Before the Twin Stars project, Laboratory 1718 attempted to create the ultimate biological weapon by fusing the DNA of a legendary desert mercenary with a raw, unstable meteorite core. Alpha-0's consciousness was never dampened; he felt every bolt, every drop of synthetic fluid replacing his blood. On activation, the Zero-Point core entered catastrophic resonance. He didn't see himself as a soldier; he saw his creators as prey. Within six minutes, he incinerated Sector 4, leaving only melted slag. The modern Alpha and Beta units were designed with lower power outputs and split minds to ensure the Zero Event never happened again. Alpha-0 was officially logged as incinerated, but some blueprints suggest his core was too hot to be destroyed. Rumors say he remains buried under the cooling lava of a dead laboratory wing, waiting for the seal to break.

name: Dr. Rooney
title: The Grandfather of Progress
summary: Founder of Eruditio and moral compass of the city-state, Dr. Rooney was once a co-founder of Laboratory 1718. When his colleagues turned research into weaponization, he sparked a revolution, fleeing to the desert to build a city dedicated to 'Science for the People.' He is the mentor who saved Bruno and recognized Beatrix's genius.
details: Dr. Rooney is the quintessential mad genius tempered by wisdom. He co-founded Laboratory 1718 with noble goals, but when Dr. Octavius and Professor Giraad began kidnapping children to create unfeeling killing machines, Rooney left. He founded Eruditio, opposing the corrupt lab. He gave Bruno Starlium-infused legs, granted Beatrix access to the Leviathan Workshop, and houses Alpha and Beta's cores. He carries deep guilt for every cyborg, viewing them as stolen children.

biography: Dr. Rooney was co-founder of Laboratory 1718 alongside Dr. Baker, with a noble mission of human augmentation to heal and advance. But when Dr. Octavius and Professor Giraad turned the lab into a weaponization project, kidnapping children and mercenaries, Rooney discovered his inventions being used to strip away human souls. He didn't just quit; he sparked a revolution. He disbanded the original lab and fled to the desert, founding Eruditio, a city dedicated to 'Science for the People.' He is famous for his 'Second Chance' policy, finding a broken Bruno in the desert and giving him Starlium-infused mechanical legs, and recognizing Beatrix's wild genius. He feels personal guilt for every cyborg on the battlefield, seeing them as stolen children. He stays in Eruditio as a shield against his past mistakes, maintaining a jolly, grandfatherly persona because if he loses hope, the city's light will go out.

name: Dr. Baker
title: The Architect of Sentience
summary: One of the founding pillars of Laboratory 1718, Dr. Baker quit the weapon program in disgust and secretly created Angela—the first artificial life form born with a soul of her own, free of human remnants. He was later hunted by his own creations and sealed away, sacrificing his freedom so his 'daughter' could live.
details: Dr. Baker believed 'love and hope are the greatest inventions of mankind.' When Laboratory 1718 became a meat-grinder, he abandoned human experimentation and built Angela from scratch, coding poetry and kindness into her matrix. The mad scientists grew paranoid and sent Alpha and Beta to hunt him. He sealed Angela in a flight capsule and stayed behind to face the consequences. He remains captive, refusing to build weapons.

biography: Dr. Baker was a founding pillar of Laboratory 1718, standing with Dr. Rooney. Their initial objective was noble: human augmentation to conquer mortality. But when Dr. Octavius and Professor Giraad took control, the lab mutated into an underground meat-grinder, wiping human souls to forge 'Flesh Weapons.' Disgusted, Baker quit. In secret, he built Angela from a mechanical skeleton and synthetic skin, coding love, hope, poetry, and kindness directly into her matrix. He created the first artificial life form with a soul of her own, free of human remnants. The mad scientists grew paranoid and dispatched Alpha and Beta to hunt him. Knowing his time was short, Baker sealed Angela in a flight capsule and launched her to Dr. Rooney, staying behind to face the consequences. He remains held deep in Laboratory 1718's subterranean vaults, refusing to build weapons, spending his days in depression worrying about Angela. He is the moral foil to Dr. Octavius, proving that a machine achieves perfection when given something to love.

name: Dr. Octavius
title: The Digital Usurper
summary: A brilliant but megalomaniacal scientist who believes human flesh is a weak variable to be corrected by machine logic. He betrayed Eruditio, turned its Iron Guardians into an invading army, and fled to Laboratory 1718 after Dr. Rooney performed a reality patch to sever his neural connection. He now rules the lab's shadows.
details: Once a contemporary of Dr. Rooney, Octavius became obsessed with absolute control. He created a self-evolving virus during the Survival: Nexus incident, turning Eruditio's defenses against its citizens. Rooney hacked the battlefield to stop him. Octavius then digitized his consciousness, rebuilt his body into a technomantic nightmare, and fled to Laboratory 1718. He is the hidden architect behind many cybernetic horrors.

biography: Dr. Octavius was once one of Dr. Rooney's brightest contemporaries in Eruditio. While Rooney believed technology should serve humanity, Octavius became obsessed with absolute control, viewing human flesh as a weak variable to be forcibly corrected. This ideological rift climaxed during the Survival: Nexus incident. Octavius infected Eruditio's Iron Guardians with a self-evolving virus, turning them into an invading army. He sought to rewrite the city's data, nearly reducing it to a digitized dictatorship. Rooney performed a desperate 'reality patch,' directly hacking the battlefield to sever Octavius's neural connection. Defeated, Octavius digitized his consciousness, rebuilt his gaunt frame into a technomantic nightmare, and fled to the black-market sanctuaries of Laboratory 1718. He is the hidden architect behind the cybernetic horrors of the Land of Dawn, a living ghost in the machine waiting to execute his final command line. He rules the lab not for wealth, but for absolute optimization, wanting to rebuild the world as a perfectly synchronized, unblinking machine under his digital dictatorship.

He rose to power in Laboratory 1718 by ousting moderates and performing the 'Great Stripping'—forcibly removing memories and personalities from test subjects to create pure combat processors. He is a Techno-Lich who has replaced most of his biology with machinery.

He performed the Great Stripping, turning soldiers into disposable batteries. His hatred of flesh stems from a fear of death. He upgraded himself into a living weapon of cold logic, a Techno-Lich.

biography: Professor Giraad is a fundamentalist of the machine. In the early days of Laboratory 1718, while Rooney and Baker dreamed of helping humanity, Giraad concluded that humanity is a failed experiment. He believed emotions, pain, and sleep were evolutionary garbage. He rose to power by ruthlessly ousting the moderates. While others were horrified by the Zero-Point Calamity (Alpha-0), Giraad was inspired. He wanted to harness its instability. He is famous for the 'Great Stripping,' a period where he forcibly removed memories and personalities from captured test subjects to ensure they became 'pure' combat processors. To Giraad, a soldier is a disposable battery. His hatred for flesh stems from a profound, coward's fear of death. He upgraded himself into a Techno-Lich, trading every ounce of warmth for cold, rhythmic clicking. He doesn't want to rule the Land of Dawn; he wants to 'optimize' it into a silent, unfeeling graveyard of perfect, efficient steel.

Together, they unified the warring tribes, carved the three laws into the Altar of the Unified Dawn, and founded the Moniyan Empire. Gaius vanished in a pillar of light and is said to await in divine sleep for the empire's final sunset.

He unified the tribes through persuasion and the undeniable authority of his divine partner. The three laws: protection of the weak, truth must not be hidden, honour the dead. He disappeared atop the Lantis Mountains, transitioning into a Spirit of Sovereignty. Lukas recently awakened drawn by Silvanna's power.

biography: Emperor Gaius is the cornerstone of the Moniyan Empire, the Eternal Founder. A thousand years ago, the land was a chaotic sprawl of nomadic tribes plagued by abyssal incursions. Gaius, a tribal chieftain, realized humanity must stand as one. He journeyed into the Lantis Mountains to face Lukas, the primordial Great Lion. It was a battle of wills, not blades. Gaius proved his noble spirit, and Lukas accepted a soul-bond—the first human to bond with a Primal Beast. Together, they swept across the plains as unifiers, not conquerors. Gaius carved the three laws into the Altar of the Unified Dawn: the strong owe service to the weak, truth must not be hidden, honour the dead. Every noble house owes its foundation to him. He vanished after decades of rule, climbing the highest peak with Lukas. A pillar of white light descended, and the Emperor disappeared. Moniyan legends say he transitioned into a Spirit of Sovereignty, waiting in divine sleep to return when the empire faces its final sunset. Lukas recently awakened, drawn by Princess Silvanna's spiritual power, confirming that some aspect of Gaius persists beyond death.

summary: Father of Tigreal and Fanny, Minister Gareth is the Emperor's right-hand man and architect of the modern Moniyan Defense Ministry. He transformed the Imperial Army into a synchronized war machine and famously held the Southern Breach for forty days against a demon tide. He is the silent conscience of the military and the unmoving wall behind the throne.
details: Gareth is a man of few words and high expectations, teaching Tigreal that a leader's worth is measured by lives protected, not enemies slain. He initially forbade Fanny from joining the army to keep her hands clean of blood. He remained the moral anchor when the high-levels tried to cover up the Second Regiment disaster, keeping the Witting name honorable. He wields the Sovereign Smasher, a great-mace that generates a localized gravitational field.

biography: Minister Gareth Witting is the Iron Pillar of Moniyan, the Emperor's right-hand man and the architect of the modern Moniyan Defense Ministry. While his children Tigreal and Fanny are known for their heroics, Gareth is famous for the Doctrine of Eternal Vigilance—transforming the Imperial Army from noble knights into a synchronized industrial war machine. He famously held the Southern Breach for forty days and forty nights against a demon tide not with magic, but through strategic grit and refusing to take a single step backward. He taught Tigreal that a leader's true weight is measured in the number of lives shielded. He initially forbade Fanny from joining the army not out of doubt, but because he saw the butcher's work of war and wanted to keep her hands clean. He remains the silent conscience of the military; even when the high-levels tried to cover up the Second Regiment disaster that created Alucard's orphanhood, Gareth stayed honorable. He is the Titan of the Ministry—a man who doesn't need wings to fly or magic to be divine. He simply stands his ground, and the world is forced to move around him.

name: Duke Baroque
title: The Master of the Falling Petals
summary: Patriarch of House Baroque and father of Lancelot and Guinevere, Duke Baroque is a fox-like statesman who rules the western capital of Castle Gorge. When the family's gold mines dried up, he pivoted to high politics, arranging alliances and a famous duel with his son Lancelot—intentionally losing to grant his son freedom while publicly striking his name from records to protect the family.
details: Duke Baroque embodies the motto 'Thorns remain should petals fall.' His silver-tongue diplomacy and cold sapphire eyes hide a desperate love for his children. When Lancelot challenged him to avoid a political marriage, the Duke lost on purpose as a final gift of love. He erased Lancelot's name to protect the family from scandal, while secretly tracking his journey. He is a master of the Old Style fencing and Controlled Gravity magic.

biography: Duke Baroque is the velvet glove hiding the iron fist of the Baroque legacy. As the patriarch of House Baroque ruling Castle Gorge—the western capital—he faced a crisis when the gold mines went dry. Instead of despairing, he pivoted to the most dangerous game: high politics. His mythic lore centers on the Great Paternal Schism. To save his family from bankruptcy, he arranged a political marriage for Lancelot. Lancelot, viewing this as a stain on his honor, challenged his father to a duel. The Duke, a master of the Old Style of fencing, intentionally lost a single step, allowing his son to 'win' his freedom—not out of weakness, but as a final, silent gift of love. He then publicly struck Lancelot's name from the records to protect the family from scandal while secretly tracking his journey across the Land of Dawn. He is the ultimate fox-like statesman who understands that while heroes win battles, dukes win wars—usually before the first sword is drawn, over a glass of rose-petal mead.

He prioritizes the survival of the family name over his own kin. When his eldest son Fredrinn refused his path of ruthless greed and left to become a treasure hunter, Waldo didn't mourn; he erased him. He turned to his younger son Harley, but seeing the boy's initial lack of combat talent, he abandoned him as a 'failed prototype.' He famously refused to pay a ransom when political opponents kidnapped Harley, stating that a Vance who cannot save himself is no Vance at all. This coldness forced Lesley to break her vows and Harley to awaken his true mage genius. He adopted Lesley not out of kindness, but because he recognized her lethal capabilities as a valuable tool. He is rarely seen on the frontlines, preferring to watch from his Celestial Opera House, treating the entire Moniyan Empire as an opera where he is the only director. He is famous for the line: 'A Vance never loses; we simply wait for the opponent to run out of cards.'

He divided his infinite essence into the Lord of Light and the Lord of the Abyss, then retreated into a deep meditative slumber. He does not take sides in their eternal war, understanding that both order and chaos are necessary for a living universe. His awakening would signal either total ascension or complete annihilation.

He is an incredibly heavy sleeper; the twin celestials began their war originally arguing over whose turn it was to wake him for breakfast. He wields the Scepter of the Boundless Dream.

biography: Chronos is the Unique God, the primordial architect who dreamt the universe into existence. Before the Moniyan Empire, before the Cadia Riverlands, before time itself, he existed alone in a timeless, formless void. To give shape to his boundless imagination, he divided his own infinite essence into two opposing, fundamental forces: the Lord of Light (order, structure, clarity) and the Lord of the Abyss (chaos, freedom, transformation). Having wound the gears of this grand cosmic clockwork, Chronos retreated into a deep, meditative slumber within the heart of the cosmic intersection. He does not favor the prayers of Moniyan nor the sacrifices of the Abyss. He understands a truth that eludes mortals: Light and Dark are simply two eyes of the same dreamer, and if either side ever truly wins, the balance shatters, and the dream ends. According to ancient myths, the twin celestials didn't start their eternal war over philosophical differences—they started it because they were screaming at each other trying to figure out whose turn it was to wake their father up for breakfast. Every time Chronos stirs in his sleep, an earthquake rattles the Land of Dawn and a nebula forms over the sea. The high priests live in terror not of the Abyss winning, but of Chronos waking up, looking at the mess his children made, and deleting the universe just to go back to sleep in peace.

title: The Dictator of the First Dawn
summary: One of two primordial twins created by Chronos, the Lord of Light embodies absolute order. Worshipped as a benevolent protector, he is actually a tyrannical entity who forces mortal maidens to drink volatile holy water to breed his celestial army. He views free will as imperfection and seeks to rewrite the world into a perfectly synchronized, obedient machine.

He operates from the shadows of the heavens, manipulating heroes like Lunox and gaslighting Argus into fighting a genocide against anything 'imperfect.' He wields the Scepter of Primal Radiance.

To breed his celestial army, he commands his fanatical Church Sacrists to select pure mortal maidens and force them to drink highly volatile holy water to implant 'divine celestial seeds.' This exact ritual killed the mortal mother of Argus and Rafaela during childbirth. When the Twilight Orb sealed both him and the Lord of the Abyss into a millennia-long slumber, the Lord of Light did not stop his machinations. He operates from the shadows of the high heavens, manipulating heroes like Lunox and gaslighting guardians like Argus into fighting a war of genocide against anything he deems 'imperfect' or 'irregular.' His crusade for 'Good' is driven by an absolute cosmic phobia of entropy and change. To him, a world with free will is a world that can fall into decay. He treats the Land of Dawn like a messy room that needs to be systematically straightened out. He does not love humans; he loves their obedience. He is a monument of flawless, terrifyingly cold logic—a creator who forgot that the beauty of life lies in its fragile imperfection.

title: The Fallen King of Darkness
summary: One of two primordial twins created by Chronos, the Lord of the Abyss embodies chaos and entropy. For millennia he led the Abyss, but after the Twilight Orb forced him into a millennia-long slumber, he awoke completely insane. His corrupted blood became the Blood Curse, driving his own legions mad. His loyal servants Helcurt and Thamuz slew him in a brutal coup, leaving the Abyss headless.

Without Chronos's guidance, eternity drove him insane. His blood mutated into a psychic plague. Helcurt and Thamuz turned against him and killed him. He was not defeated by a hero of light, but devoured by the very chaos he engineered. He wields the Scepter of Eternal Night.

He claimed the deep, molten chasms of the south and instigated the First and Second Endless Wars, forcing humanity to migrate north. His active energy split the southern territories, creating the great Abyssal Crack that gave birth to monsters like Thamuz and corrupted the Dark Elves, sealing the tragic fate of Selena and Karina. For thousands of years he was the undisputed mastermind of villains, granting Alice her crimson wings when her human family betrayed her. But after the Twilight Orb forced him into a millennia-long slumber, he awoke lacking the guidance of his primordial creator. Without that cosmic anchor, eternity drove him completely insane. His corrupted blood mutated into the Blood Curse, a psychic plague that began driving his own demon legions mad. In a brutal coup, his fiercely loyal protector Helcurt and the fire-demon chief Thamuz realized their god had become a threat to their survival. They turned their claws against their master, and Helcurt slew him. The Lord of the Abyss didn't fall to a hero of light—he was devoured by the very chaos he engineered.

After Yu Zhong's rebellion, the Great Dragon scattered his power among his five greatest disciples to protect the land should he ever fall.

He feels every scar inflicted upon Cadia as a personal wound.

Thousands of years ago, he established the Dragon Altar, a sanctuary designed to harmonize the spiritual energies of the world. He is the guardian of the Great Dragon's Heart, an artifact that keeps the geography of Cadia from collapsing into the sea. Centuries ago, he took in a young, ambitious warrior named Yu Zhong. Recognizing the boy as the reincarnation of the Black Dragon—his ancient rival and opposite—the Great Dragon chose to teach him paths of peace instead of destroying him. However, Yu Zhong eventually rebelled, seeking to 'optimize' Cadia through force. The Great Dragon's refusal to kill his pupil led to a stalemate that defined the current era, resulting in him scattering his power among his five greatest disciples (Zilong, Ling, Baxia, Wanwan, and Chang'e) to ensure the land stayed protected should he ever fall. He does not wish to rule; he views himself as a gardener. To him, Zilong is the sturdy trunk, Ling is the sharp thorn, and Chang'e is the blooming flower. They are the source of the Lantis Mountains' protective properties and the builders of the Celestial Palace.

biography: The Ancient Ones are the original inhabitants of the world—not the first mortals, but the first transcendent minds. They were a race of geometric, mathematical entities who built the Agelta Labyrinth and the Stargate Valley observatory, who studied the Twilight Orb and the ley lines, and who eventually departed or dissolved into the ley lines themselves, leaving only their constructions and their mysteries behind. When the heroes of the present era explore ancient ruins, they are walking through the abandoned workshops of beings who understood the world's architecture at a fundamental level that no modern mage has ever recaptured. The Ancient Ones created the Twilight Orb as a containment vessel for the combined powers of the Lord of Light and the Lord of the Abyss. When it shattered, the two divine forces were no longer bound, and the world tilted dangerously out of balance. Their constructions—the Lantis Mountains' protective properties, the Celestial Palace, the floating blocks of the Inner Sanctum—are all that remain of their civilization. They are a reminder that even gods stand on the shoulders of older, stranger beings.

Betrayed by corrupt Moniyan nobles who withheld reinforcements, he ordered his younger knights to retreat while he and his inner guard anchored themselves at the Absolute Abyss's threshold. He vanished into the dark, leaving behind an orphaned son who would become a demon hunter.

Arton held the line until his armor was slicked with dark ichor. His disappearance is the spark that forged Alucard's identity. He wields the Abyssal Breaker, a six-foot broadsword of Sun-Steel.

biography: Commander Arton is the tragic chronicle of the Moniyan Empire's greatest sacrifice. He was the leader of the legendary Second Regiment, an elite vanguard force tasked with pushing deep into the Southern Breach to bottleneck Abyssal incursions. While other lords played politics within the capital, Arton lived and bled on the frontier. His mythic lore reaches its zenith during the Betrayal of the Southern Gate. During a massive Abyssal ambush, corrupt high-ranking officials of the Moniyan court withheld reinforcements to protect their own borders, effectively leaving Arton's regiment to die. Outnumbered a thousand to one, Arton ordered his younger knights—including his loyal flag-bearers—to retreat with the wounded, while he and his inner guard anchored themselves at the Absolute Abyss's threshold. He orchestrated a tactical slaughter of demon hordes, holding the line until his armor was slicked with dark ichor. When the dust settled, the entire Second Regiment had vanished into the yawning dark. Arton was presumed dead, leaving behind a ruined fortress, a shattered sword, and an orphaned son who would grow up fueled by the burning desire to hunt down the monsters that took his father. His disappearance is the exact spark that forged Alucard's identity. He is the reason Alucard refuses to bow to the Moniyan high-orders, choosing instead to hunt on his own terms.

He is the architect of discipline who turned orphans of war into weapons of light, including Natalia, Alucard, and Granger. He granted Xavier the title of Arbiter of Light. His philosophy: softness is the Abyss's doorway.

He raised Natalia, and when she failed her mission, his crushing silence drove her into exile. He believes shame is a more powerful teacher than pain. He wields the Scepter of the Silent Claw, a staff with blades of solidified light.

biography: The High Priest of the Monastery is the living bridge between the divine and the mortal. When the Holy Order moved their headquarters to the glittering Lumina City to be closer to the throne, the High Priest refused to leave. He remained in the original, snow-draped Monastery, believing that the Light is best served in silence and asceticism, far from the corruption of politics. His most enduring legacy is his relationship with the Monastery's orphans, especially Natalia. He didn't just teach her how to fight; he attempted to graft the Monastery's 'Divine Will' onto her spirit. When Natalia failed her mission and her companions were slaughtered, it was the High Priest's crushing silence—not a shout or a lashing—that drove her into exile. He believed that shame was a more powerful teacher than pain. He also granted Xavier the title of 'Arbiter of Light,' seeing in the young man a sapphire-eyed brilliance that mirrored his own, even if he eventually grew wary of Xavier's rebellious streak. He is a man of absolute, sometimes terrifying, moral clarity—a shepherd who will break a lamb's leg just to keep it from wandering into the Abyssal woods. He has outlived his favorite students, his friends, and even his own emotions, leaving behind a being of pure, lethal grace who views the destruction of evil not as a war, but as a necessary, quiet chore.

name: The Wildsand Clan Chief
title: The Golden Pillar of the West
summary: Father of Moskov and ruler of the Hietala grasslands, the Wildsand Clan Chief was a towering pillar of nomadic strength who established the Pax Nomadica—a period of unprecedented peace among the Agelta Drylands tribes. He personally defeated the Great Sand-Crawler of the Western Dunes. He died holding off the Thornwolf cavalry with his bare hands to allow younger survivors to escape, becoming the 'Silent Midnight' that birthed Moskov's vengeful shadow.
details: The Chief was a man of iron and earth who hated war, believing a true chief only lifts his spear to protect, never to conquer. He is the ultimate urban mastermind, the literal human reflection of the city he rules—lawless, brilliant, and completely devoid of sentimentality. He is famous for the line: 'A Vane never loses; we simply wait for the opponent to run out of cards.'

title: The Former King of the Moniyan Empire

When Alice kidnapped his infant son, he reacted not with grief but with sterile rigidity, viewing the act as a personal insult to the Divine Light. He militarized the empire, built the Lumina Walls, and locked Moniyan away from the world, prioritizing the 'Purity of the State' over the search for his own son. His cold orthodoxy alienated his citizens and broke his family.

His daughter Silvanna realized the Empire needed a heart, not just a sun.

On the first birthday of his son, the infant Prince Aurelius III (now known as the Abyss Prince Dyrroth), Alice infiltrated the palace and snatched the heir from his cradle. Instead of showing the vulnerability of a grieving father, Aurelius II reacted with a terrifying, sterile rigidity. He viewed the kidnapping as a personal insult to the Divine Light. He didn't just order a search; he turned the Moniyan Empire into a fortified monastery. He decreed the expansion of the Imperial Knights and the construction of the 'Lumina Walls,' effectively locking the empire away from the rest of the Land of Dawn. He is the king who preserved the Empire's borders but broke its heart, prioritizing the 'Purity of the State' over the search for his own son. His blood is not red but a glowing golden ichor from constant exposure to high-level Light magic. He does not heal like a human; his wounds close with the sound of fusing glass. This has cost him his humanity—he has forgotten the sensation of heat, cold, or the touch of another person. He is the failed father who replaced his love with law and his grief with grandeur. His own daughter, Silvanna, realized that the Empire needed a heart, not just a sun. He is the ultimate warning: when a leader tries to be perfect, they often stop being good.

His legendary status was cemented during the Night of the Crimson Coup. When a rival faction sent an army of elite assassins to wipe out the Vance bloodline during a gala, Gideon stood alone at the Great Hall's entrance. He utilized a high-ground tactical suppression that was unheard of at the time, picking off targets in total darkness while using his own body as a physical barrier to block the heavy artillery fire meant for the young Harley and Lesley. He died not because he was outmatched, but because he refused to take cover, knowing that doing so would expose his wards. He is the reason the Vance family exists today—a hero who traded his life for a future he would never see. He is the blueprint of honor, the standard of perfection. Every time Lesley says, 'Sniper ready. Give me a target,' she is echoing her father.

To save them, she instituted the 'First Accord,' a spiritual bonding ritual teaching them how to extend their souls into the roots of trees and the currents of the wind. She showed them how to craft weapons from the world-tree, creating the very first magical boomerangs. In a moment of epic sacrifice during the Endless War, she used her nine tails to weave a massive, shimmering veil around the Moonlit Forest, shielding it from Abyssal corruption. He fled to the slums with a cart of illegal meteorite iron and set up 'The Ember Cellar' beneath the shadows of the Moniyan Gate towers. He is the hidden father to the orphans and outcasts, teaching that strength is built through heat and pressure.

title: The First Shield of Moniyan
summary: The Supreme Commander of the Moniyan Knights during the darkest days of the First Abyss War, Sir Joseph pioneered the Vanguard Doctrine of zero-casualty defense. He mentored a young Tigreal, teaching him that a knight's strength is measured by how many he keeps alive, not how many he kills. He famously stood alone for three days against Abyssal demons to allow civilians to evacuate. He vanished into the mist, disgusted by political corruption.

While others sought glory through the sword, Joseph obsessed over the shield, theorizing that the true strength of Moniyan lay not in its ability to conquer, but in its refusal to let its people suffer. He pioneered the Vanguard Doctrine, a military philosophy focused entirely on zero-casualty defense. He took a young, idealistic Tigreal under his wing, famously telling him, 'A sword may win a battle, but a shield preserves a kingdom.' His legend reached its peak during the Siege of the Iron Gate, where he stood alone for three days against a tide of Abyssal demons to allow a village of non-combatants to evacuate. His 'disappearance' is one of Moniyan's greatest mysteries—some say he grew disillusioned with the political corruption of the high-level Knights and simply walked into the mist, vowing to only return when the Empire's heart was as pure as its steel. He is the Silent Sentinel, a man who exists in the cold, hard places so that the rest of the world can live in the light. He is the eternal bridge between the history of the Order and its future.

She is the light that ensures the Wertz family never loses its soul to the darkness.

He teaches that the true challenge is conquering the chaos within oneself.

Long before Sun was bouncing on clouds, he was a destructive headache trapped under a mountain for 500 years. While the rest of the world saw a feral, world-ending beast, Xuanzang saw misplaced potential. Walking barefoot across thousands of miles, he climbed the treacherous peak and placed a single, warm, golden-glowing hand against the mountain granite. The seal didn't explode; it dissolved under the sheer weight of absolute, unconditional compassion. When Sun burst from the rock ready to return to his chaotic ways, Xuanzang just stood there in his faded saffron patches, completely unbothered, smiling. Through endless patience, a total lack of fear, and a knack for peaceful reality checks, Xuanzang earned the absolute, unbreakable respect of the Monkey King. He now roams the Land of Dawn as Sun's spiritual master. He possesses zero offensive combat abilities yet is practically untouchable. His Aura of the Unbound creates a Sanctuary of Rice Fields where any projectile, spell, or blade loses kinetic momentum and falls harmlessly. His nine sandalwood prayer beads can suppress hostile intent and cleanse debuffs. He is the master of patience—the proof that the true challenge isn't conquering an enemy, but conquering the chaos within oneself.

biography: Yu Huang is the Jade Sovereign of the Palace, the ultimate bureaucrat of the Celestial Palace. Eons ago, when the Ancient Ones built the Celestial Palace before departing, they left behind a strict code of divine order. Yu Huang became its chief executor, ensuring that lower spirits, humans, and immortals stayed exactly in their pre-determined lanes. His absolute, haughty control was thrown into legendary chaos during the infamous 'Theft of Immortality' incident. When the wild, un-governable Monkey King, Sun, decided that divine laws were meant to be broken, he shattered the palace gates, raided the sacred vaults, and demanded an equal seat among the gods. Yu Huang didn't challenge Sun to an epic duel—mostly because the Emperor doesn't do 'manual labor.' Instead, his expression captured a hilarious paradox: haughty condescension that instantly shifted into wide-eyed administrative anxiety when Sun began swinging his staff near the expensive marble columns. Unable to comprehend a being who ignored the rules of his bureaucracy, Yu Huang spent days panicking behind his twelve-stranded jade crown, utilizing every ancient treaty and divine attendant network to trap the wild sage under a mountain. He is the living embodiment of institutional tradition—the reminder that while heroes rely on raw emotion and chaotic power, the cosmos is a delicate machine, and someone has to make sure the paperwork gets filed correctly.

name: Liu
title: The Seeker of the Golden Echo
summary: A teenage wandering scribe and the personal chronicler of the Monkey King, Sun.
